title: Macanese Minchi with Crispy Potatoes and Fried Eggs
blurb: Macau's great comfort dish: soy-and-Worcestershire beef tangled with craggy fried potato cubes and crowned with a lacy fried egg.

ingredients.item: 1 lb Simply Nature Organic Grass-Fed Ground Beef
3 cups Season's Choice frozen diced breakfast potatoes
3 tbsp Fusia Asian Inspirations soy sauce
1 tsp Mushroom & Company Multipurpose Umami Seasoning Blend

steps.text: Film a large nonstick skillet with olive oil and set it over medium-high until the surface shimmers and thins out. Scatter the frozen potatoes in a single loose layer and walk away so the undersides can blister and turn deep gold.
steps.tip: Crowding steams them

steps.text: Toss the potatoes and keep cooking until most faces are crackly and browned, then scrape them onto a plate and salt them while they are hot. Dice the onion and mince the garlic while they finish.
Return the empty skillet to medium-high, add the beef, and press it into one flat slab. Leave it completely undisturbed until the underside forms a dark brown crust that releases from the pan.

Break the beef into rough pebbles with a wooden spoon, then add the onion, garlic, and bay leaves. Stir often until the onion turns translucent at the edges and the garlic smells toasty rather than sharp.

Pour in the soy sauce and Worcestershire, then sprinkle over the brown sugar and umami seasoning. Simmer over medium until the liquid tightens into a dark glaze that clings to the meat instead of pooling.
steps.tip: Glaze, don't drown

steps.text: While the beef glazes, microwave the frozen jasmine rice according to the bag and fluff it with a fork. Fold the crisped potatoes back into the beef right at the end so they stay crunchy.
In a small nonstick pan over medium heat, fry the eggs in a slick of olive oil until the whites are opaque all the way through and the edges go frilly and brown but the yolks still tremble.
Fish out the bay leaves, spoon the minchi over the rice, and slide an egg onto each plate. Finish with the sliced scallions and a last few drops of Worcestershire.

swap: If the frozen diced potatoes are sold out, cut two russets into small cubes, parboil them for a few minutes, and pat them very dry before frying.
leftovers: Refrigerate the beef and potatoes together up to three days and reheat in a dry hot skillet so the potato edges crisp back up before you fry a fresh egg.

title: Sindhi Seyal Murgh, Smothered in Garlic and Cilantro
blurb: Chicken braised down into a fistful of garlic, split green chilies, and an almost indecent amount of cilantro until the masala clings tight to every piece.

ingredients.item: 1.5 lb Kirkwood boneless skinless chicken thighs, halved
1 large bunch cilantro, tender stems and leaves, roughly chopped
8 cloves garlic, half minced and half smashed
1/2 cup Friendly Farms plain Greek yogurt

steps.text: Pat the chicken very dry, salt it well, and rub it with the turmeric and red chili powder until every piece is stained yellow. Let it sit while you chop the cilantro, garlic, and tomatoes.
steps.tip: Dry chicken, better sear

steps.text: Heat three tablespoons of olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high, then add the cumin seeds. Wait until they sizzle steadily, darken a shade, and smell nutty before moving on.
steps.tip: Smell them, don't scorch them

steps.text: Lay the chicken in one uncrowded layer and leave it alone until the undersides are burnished gold and lift cleanly. Flip once and sear the second side.
Add the minced and smashed garlic, the ginger, and the split green chilies. Stir constantly so the garlic goes pale gold and loses its raw bite without burning.
Tip in the tomatoes and crush them against the pan. Cook over medium until they collapse into a thick paste and you see oil beading at the edges of the masala.
steps.tip: Oil separating means the masala is ready

steps.text: Drop the heat to medium-low and stir in the yogurt one spoonful at a time so it never breaks. Cover and simmer until the chicken is fork tender and the sauce has darkened.

Pile in the whole chopped bunch of cilantro and the garam masala, then fold until the greens wilt down and the sauce is thick enough to cling rather than run. Char the naan in a dry skillet while it finishes.
Let the pan rest off the heat so the masala tightens, then serve straight from the skillet with the hot naan for scooping.

swap: No fresh green chilies at the store? Use a spoonful of Green Dragon Hot Sauce stirred in with the yogurt for the same grassy heat.
leftovers: This tastes even better on day two once the garlic mellows; store it up to three days and reheat gently with a splash of water to loosen the masala.

title: Venetian Shrimp in Saor over Soft Parmesan Polenta
blurb: Sweet-sour saor onions slumped in vinegar with raisins and pine nuts, spooned over seared red shrimp and a warm pool of parmesan polenta.

ingredients.item: 1 lb Raw Argentinian Red Shrimp, thawed and peeled
2 large red onions, halved and sliced thin

steps.text: Warm a generous slick of olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-low, then add the sliced onions, bay leaves, and a big pinch of salt. Cook, stirring now and then, until the onions collapse into soft ribbons that are sweet and barely blond.
steps.tip: Low and slow keeps them sweet, not brown

steps.text: While the onions soften, bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil for the polenta and pat the shrimp completely dry on paper towels.

Pour the vinegar into the onions and add the raisins and sugar. Simmer until the sharp vinegar smell mellows into something rounded and the pan looks glossy and nearly syrupy, then stir in the pine nuts.
Rain the polenta into the boiling water while whisking hard so no lumps form, then drop the heat to low. Whisk often until it thickens enough to pull away from the side of the pot.
Beat the parmesan and butter into the polenta until it is loose and creamy, taste for salt, and cover it off the heat so it stays soft.

Toss the dry shrimp with the flour, salt, and pepper. Sear them in one layer in a hot oiled skillet over medium-high until they turn coral pink, curl into loose C shapes, and are opaque at the thickest part.
steps.tip: Argentinian reds cook fast, watch closely

steps.text: Kill the heat, spoon the warm saor over the shrimp, and toss so every piece is coated. Let the pan sit so the vinegar and sweetness soak in.
steps.tip: The rest is what makes it saor

steps.text: Spread the polenta across two warm shallow bowls, pile on the shrimp and onions with all their syrup, and scatter the parsley over the top.

swap: If pine nuts are out of stock, slivered almonds toasted in a dry pan give the same sweet crunch against the vinegar.
leftovers: The saor shrimp are traditionally eaten cold the next day; keep them chilled up to two days and eat them straight from the fridge on toasted bread.

title: Honduran Tapado: Garifuna Coconut Chicken and Shrimp Stew
blurb: A Caribbean-coast pot from Honduras where coconut milk simmers gold with cumin and lime until chicken, plantain, and sweet red shrimp fall together.

ingredients.item: 2.5 lb Kirkwood boneless skinless chicken thighs
1 lb Raw Argentinian Red Shrimp, peeled
2 green plantains, peeled and cut into thick coins

steps.text: Season the chicken all over with salt and half the cumin. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high and brown the thighs in two batches, undisturbed, until each side wears a deep golden crust.
steps.tip: Two batches, or it steams

steps.text: While the chicken browns, peel and cut the plantains into thick coins and halve the potatoes so everything is ready to go into the pot at once.

Move the browned chicken to a plate, drop the heat to medium, and add the onion, garlic, and fire roasted peppers and onions. Cook, scraping up the brown film on the bottom, until the onion is soft and translucent.
steps.tip: Those scraped-up bits are the flavor

steps.text: Stir in the rest of the cumin, then return the chicken with its juices and add the broth, coconut milk, potatoes, and plantains. Bring it up to a lazy simmer with slow bubbles rather than a hard boil.
steps.tip: A hard boil splits coconut milk

steps.text: Simmer partly covered until a knife slides into the potatoes with no resistance, the plantains turn tender and starchy, and the broth thickens to pale gold. Chop the cilantro and juice the limes while you wait.
Taste for salt, then slip the shrimp under the surface of the stew and cook just until they curl and turn opaque coral through the middle.
steps.tip: Pull them early, the pot keeps cooking

steps.text: Kill the heat and stir in the lime juice and half the cilantro. Let the pot rest so the coconut settles into the broth and the flavors knit together.
Ladle into deep bowls, making sure every serving gets chicken, shrimp, plantain, and potato. Finish with the remaining cilantro and a wedge of lime.

swap: No green plantains in produce? Use a large sweet potato cut into thick chunks and add it with the baby potatoes.
leftovers: Store up to four days; reheat over low heat only until steaming so the shrimp stay tender, and freeze portions before adding the shrimp if you want them perfect later.

title: Balinese Sate Lilit Chicken with Sambal Matah
blurb: Lemongrass and coconut chicken patties charred hard in a skillet, then buried under raw sambal matah that hisses when the hot coconut oil hits it.

steps.text: Mix the ground chicken with the shredded coconut, two tablespoons of the lemongrass paste, the garlic, turmeric, coconut milk, and a heavy pinch of salt. Work it with your hands until it turns tacky and holds its shape when you squeeze a lump, then chill it.
steps.tip: Tacky mix means the patties won't crumble

steps.text: Build the sambal matah while the mixture chills: toss the shallots, chilies, remaining lemongrass paste, the zest and juice of two limes, and salt with your fingertips, bruising the shallots as you go.
steps.tip: Bruise, don't mash

steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a small pan over medium-high until it ripples and just begins to shimmer, then pour it straight over the sambal so it sizzles on contact and stir it through.
steps.tip: Hot oil wakes the raw shallots up

steps.text: With wet hands, form the chilled chicken into eight oblong patties, pressing them into flat ovals so they sear evenly rather than steam.
Heat a cast iron skillet over medium-high, film it with oil, and lay the patties in without crowding. Leave them completely alone until the undersides build a dark brown, almost charred crust.
Flip, lower the heat to medium, and cook until the patties feel springy in the middle and the juices run clear with no pink at the center.
Heat the frozen jasmine rice while the patties finish, then fluff it and dust it with the Chili Lime Seasoning.
Pile the rice into bowls, lean the charred patties against it, and heap the sambal matah over everything with its oil. Serve with the last lime cut into wedges.

swap: If lemongrass paste is missing, finely mince the pale bottom of two fresh lemongrass stalks, or use the zest of an extra lime plus a little grated ginger.
leftovers: Keep the patties and sambal in separate containers up to three days; reheat the patties in a skillet and spoon the cold sambal over at the last second.

title: Austrian Pork Schnitzel with Warm Vinegar Potato Salad
blurb: Shatteringly crisp, puffed golden schnitzel with a hard squeeze of lemon, next to warm Erdapfelsalat slick with mustard, vinegar, and shaved red onion.

ingredients.item: 1/2 small red onion, shaved paper thin

steps.text: Start the potatoes first: cover them with heavily salted water, bring to a boil, and cook until a knife slides into the middle with no resistance.
steps.tip: Salt the water like soup

steps.text: While they boil, lay the pork between two sheets of plastic wrap and pound it with a heavy pan until each cutlet is thin, even, and noticeably wider than it started.
steps.tip: Even thickness means even frying

steps.text: Set up three shallow dishes with the flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs. Season the pork, then coat each piece in flour, egg, and crumbs, pressing only lightly so the crust can puff away from the meat.
steps.tip: Press hard and the coating glues down

steps.text: Drain the potatoes, slice them into warm coins, and whisk the mustard, vinegar, warm broth, red onion, salt, and pepper together. Pour it over while the potatoes are still steaming and toss, then leave them to soak.
steps.tip: Dress them hot so they drink it up

steps.text: Melt half the butter with a slick of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high until the foam subsides. Lay in two cutlets and swirl the pan constantly so hot fat washes over the tops and the crust blisters and puffs golden.
steps.tip: Keep the pan moving

steps.text: Flip and fry the second side until it is the deep color of a good pretzel and the edges are crisp and ruffled.
Drain the schnitzel on a wire rack, never on paper, and salt it the second it comes out of the pan. Wipe the skillet, add the remaining butter and oil, and fry the second pair the same way.
steps.tip: A rack keeps the bottom crisp

steps.text: Fold the chives through the potato salad, taste it for vinegar and salt, and serve the schnitzel straight away with lemon wedges to squeeze over the crust.

swap: Thin-cut chicken breasts pounded the same way stand in perfectly, and a spoonful of any berry jam on the side plays the part of lingonberry.
leftovers: The potato salad keeps three days and only gets better; re-crisp leftover schnitzel in a hot dry skillet or oven rather than the microwave.

title: Tunisian Ojja with Merguez and Eggs
blurb: Tunis in a skillet: harissa and crushed caraway fried into tomatoes and peppers with spicy merguez, with eggs poached right in the fiery sauce.

ingredients.item: 12 oz merguez sausage, cut into thick coins

steps.text: Set a wide skillet over medium-high and brown the merguez coins in a bare film of olive oil until they are crusted on both cut sides and the fat runs out bright red.
steps.tip: That red fat is the whole base

steps.text: Lift the sausage out with a slotted spoon and leave the fat behind. Drop the heat to medium, add the garlic, crushed caraway, and coriander, and stir until they smell toasted but the garlic has not colored.
Stir in the tomato paste and harissa and fry them in the fat, pressing them against the pan, until the paste darkens to brick red and smells roasted instead of raw.
steps.tip: Frying the paste kills the tinny taste

steps.text: Add the fire roasted peppers and onions and the diced tomatoes with their juice. Simmer over medium until the sauce thickens enough that a spoon dragged through it leaves a trail that holds. Slice the bread and chop the parsley while it reduces.
Return the sausage and any resting juices, taste for salt, and make four shallow wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon. Crack an egg into each well and season the yolks.
Cover the pan and cook over medium-low until the whites are fully opaque and set but the yolks still wobble when you nudge the handle.
steps.tip: Pull it early, carryover finishes the yolks

steps.text: Shower the whole skillet with parsley and squeeze lemon over the top. Bring it to the table in the pan with the bread for dragging through the sauce.

swap: No merguez on the counter? Use Never Any! spicy sausage and add an extra spoonful of harissa plus a pinch more caraway to get the same North African punch.
leftovers: The sauce alone keeps four days and freezes well; reheat it in a skillet and poach fresh eggs in it rather than saving the cooked ones.

title: Bahamian Brown Stew Chicken with Thyme and Hot Pepper
blurb: Nassau-style stew chicken, where sugar burnt almost to bitterness lacquers the meat mahogany before it simmers soft with thyme, allspice, and hot sauce.

ingredients.item: 3.5 lb Kirkwood bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks

steps.text: Season the chicken hard on all sides with salt, pepper, the thyme, and the allspice, then let it sit out while you slice the onion, pepper, and celery.
steps.tip: Season early, season heavily

steps.text: In a wide Dutch oven over medium-high, stir the brown sugar into a thin film of olive oil and swirl until it melts, foams up, and turns the color of dark coffee with a faintly bitter smell.
steps.tip: This burnt sugar is the color of the whole dish

steps.text: Immediately lay in the chicken skin side down in batches, standing back because it will spit, and brown it hard, turning once, until each piece is lacquered mahogany.
Move the chicken to a tray and add the onion, bell pepper, celery, and bay leaves to the pot. Cook, scraping the dark caramel off the bottom, until the vegetables soften and go glossy.
Stir in the tomato paste and hot sauce and cook until the paste turns brick colored and coats the vegetables.

Return the chicken with every drop of its juice, add the potatoes, and pour in enough water to come halfway up the chicken. Bring it to a simmer, cover, and cook until the meat pulls easily from the bone. Heat the rice pouches near the end.
Uncover, raise the heat to medium-high, and let the liquid boil down until the gravy is dark and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
steps.tip: Taste for salt only after it reduces

steps.text: Rest the pot off the heat, fish out the bay leaves, and skim any fat from the surface. Spoon the chicken and gravy over the hot rice.

swap: If bone-in pieces are picked over, boneless thighs work; brown them the same way and cut the covered simmer roughly in half.
leftovers: This deepens overnight and keeps four days; pull the meat off the bones and reheat it in the gravy, or freeze it in portions for up to three months.
